steps.name: Build code-mode assets
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail

# Build the code-mode assets once per SDK state, not once per job. Cache volumes
# are forks of past jobs, so most jobs miss the store path another job just built.
# The key is the store path, which covers every input of the build.
assets="$(nix eval --raw .#code-mode-assets.outPath)"
echo "CODE_MODE_ASSETS_DIR=$assets" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

if nix-store --check-validity "$assets" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "Code-mode assets already in the store"
  exit 0
fi

# Forks have no remote cache credentials.
if [ -z "${SCCACHE_WEBDAV_ENDPOINT:-}" ]; then
  nix build --no-link --print-build-logs .#code-mode-assets
  exit 0
fi

cache_url="$SCCACHE_WEBDAV_ENDPOINT/code-mode-assets/$(basename "$assets").closure.gz"

# The token goes through a config descriptor so it stays out of curl's arguments.
cache_request() {
  curl --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 30 --retry 2 \
    -K <(printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "$SCCACHE_WEBDAV_TOKEN") "$@"
}

if cache_request "$cache_url" | gunzip | nix-store --import; then
  echo "Code-mode assets restored from the remote cache"
  exit 0
fi

# Installing node_modules is most of a build and changes far less often than the SDK,
# so it has its own entry.
modules="$(nix eval --raw .#macro-js-node-modules.outPath)"
modules_url="$SCCACHE_WEBDAV_ENDPOINT/code-mode-assets/$(basename "$modules").zst"
save_modules=false

if ! nix-store --check-validity "$modules" 2>/dev/null; then
  # No retries: a retry would restart the stream into the same pipe, and past the limit
  # a rebuild is faster.
  if cache_request --retry 0 --max-time 60 "$modules_url" | zstd -d | nix-store --import; then
    echo "node_modules restored from the remote cache"
  else
    save_modules=true
  fi
fi

nix build --no-link --print-build-logs .#code-mode-assets

if [ "$save_modules" = true ] \
  && ! nix-store --export "$modules" | zstd -T0 -3 | cache_request --max-time 120 --upload-file - "$modules_url"; then
  echo "::warning::Could not save node_modules to the remote cache"
fi

# Losing the upload costs the next job a rebuild, not a failure.
if nix-store --export "$assets" | gzip | cache_request --upload-file - "$cache_url"; then
  echo "Code-mode assets saved to the remote cache"
else
  echo "::warning::Could not save code-mode assets to the remote cache"
fi

steps.name: clippy
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail

# Mirrors run_tests.sh package selection so clippy only lints the crates this
# PR can actually affect. `all` keeps the historical workspace invocation,
# including sync_service's special-cased feature set.

packages="${RUST_PACKAGES:-}"

clippy_sync_service() {
  cargo clippy -p sync_service -- \
    -A clippy::unnecessary_map_or \
    -A clippy::collapsible_if
}

# Most of soup's dependents build it without `outbound` (no features, or
# `ports` alone), where helpers only the service or the Postgres repository
# call are dead code that --all-features hides.
clippy_soup_without_outbound() {
  cargo clippy -p soup --no-default-features
  cargo clippy -p soup --no-default-features --features ports
}

if [ -z "$packages" ] || [ "$packages" = "all" ]; then
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --exclude sync_service
  clippy_sync_service
  clippy_soup_without_outbound
  exit 0
fi

if [ "$packages" = "none" ]; then
  echo "No Rust packages to lint"
  exit 0
fi

sync=false
soup=false
pkg_args=()
for p in $packages; do
  if [ "$p" = "sync_service" ]; then
    sync=true
  else
    pkg_args+=(-p "$p")
  fi
  if [ "$p" = "soup" ]; then
    soup=true
  fi
done

if [ "${#pkg_args[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  cargo clippy --all-features "${pkg_args[@]}"
fi

if [ "$sync" = true ]; then
  clippy_sync_service
fi

if [ "$soup" = true ]; then
  clippy_soup_without_outbound
fi

steps.name: build service binaries
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail

: "${RUST_PACKAGES:?RUST_PACKAGES is required}"

# The test job never compiles these services' `run` bodies: each is an `impl
# Future` polled only by the bin's `main`, and a bin's test target doesn't call
# `main`. Clippy stops before monomorphization. So a failure only a real build
# finds, such as a recursion limit overflow while instantiating, shows up here.
selected=()
for service in document_storage_service email_service authentication_service; do
  if [ "$RUST_PACKAGES" = "all" ] || [[ " $RUST_PACKAGES " == *" $service "* ]]; then
    selected+=("$service")
  fi
done

if [ "${#selected[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "No service binaries were affected"
  exit 0
fi

# The same packages and features as run_tests.sh. Building each service's
# `service_binary_builds` test target, which nothing runs, makes cargo build the
# real binaries under the features `cargo test` resolves, so every other unit is
# one the test job builds too and both jobs share sccache entries. `cargo build`
# would resolve without dev-dependency features and rebuild most of the workspace.
if [ "$RUST_PACKAGES" = "all" ]; then
  package_args=(--workspace --exclude sync_service)
else
  package_args=()
  for package in $RUST_PACKAGES; do
    [ "$package" = "sync_service" ] || package_args+=(-p "$package")
  done
fi

cargo test --no-run --locked --all-features \
  --config 'profile.dev.package."*".debug=false' "${package_args[@]}" \
  --test service_binary_builds

steps.name: verify js node_modules derivation is up to date
steps.run:
# A fixed-output derivation already in the store is accepted without
# running it, whatever bun.lock now says, so only then does the check
# need a rebuild. On a store without it, the first build is the check.
out=$(nix eval --raw .#js-node-modules.outPath)
if nix-store --check-validity "$out" 2>/dev/null; then
  nix build .#js-node-modules --no-link --rebuild
else
  nix build .#js-node-modules --no-link
fi

steps.name: Check packed SDK
steps.run: bun run build && bun run check:pack

steps.name: Build the NixOS image
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
  echo "KVM is available"
else
  echo "::warning::No /dev/kvm: the image builds under QEMU emulation"
fi
features="$(nix config show system-features) kvm"
time nix build . --option system-features "$features" --print-build-logs --out-link result
du -shL result/*.vhd
